shower.thought: We spend our whole lives learning how to be ourselves, and then we die.
The most honest conversation you'll ever have might be with someone you'll never see again.
You can't remember most of your life, which means you're already a different person than you think you are.
Silence is the only thing that sounds the same to everyone.
You're nostalgic for times you didn't fully appreciate when you were living them.
If you had to describe color to someone who'd never seen it, you'd realize you don't actually know what color is.
The things you regret most are usually the things you didn't do, but you only know that because you lived through not doing them.
Forgetting something doesn't make it less true—it just makes it true in a way that no longer affects you.
Your body is mostly empty space, but it still takes up room.
We call it "falling" asleep, but you're actually rising into another world.
The scariest monsters are the ones you create to explain sounds you don't understand.
You've never actually tasted food—you've only tasted your own perception of it.
Every photo you take is proof that you weren't fully present for the moment.
The only time you're completely honest is when you're alone, which means your real self only exists in private.
Waiting for something to happen is the only way to guarantee it will happen slower.
You know the ending of every story you've ever read, but you read them anyway.
Your shadow has been following you your entire life, and you still barely know it.
The problem with living is that you can't see how it ends until it's over.
Time moves faster the less attention you pay to it.
You're more similar to a stranger than you are to yourself from ten years ago.

darkjoke.thought:
I told my friend he was being paranoid about his job security.
Turns out he was right to worry — they replaced him with me.

My therapist keeps asking about my childhood trauma.
I said, "Doc, if I wanted to relive it, I'd just call my parents."

I'm at that age where my back goes out more than I do.
Last week it didn't even ask permission.

My wife asked if I was listening to her.
I said, "Of course," which apparently was the wrong answer.

I have a stepladder because my real ladder left when I was just a kid.
It's not a very good relationship, but at least it's honest.

People say money can't buy happiness.
They've clearly never bought a flight away from their in-laws.

I asked my boss for a raise and he said the company was going through tough times.
Funny how tough times never seem to affect his parking spot.

My dad told me to follow my dreams.
So I'm in his room every night and he's furious.

I tried to tell a chemistry joke but there was no reaction.
Mostly because I'm terrible at chemistry and also a boring person.

I used to be addicted to soap.
I'm clean now.

My doctor said I need to watch my drinking.
So now I drink in front of a mirror.

I told my son that life was like a box of chocolates.
He said, "So eventually you'll be alone and slightly sticky?"

My therapist asked if I had any coping mechanisms.
I said yes and then didn't come back.

I got fired from the calendar factory for taking a day off.
They said I was a day late anyway.

My relationship is like a walk in the park.
Jurassic Park.

I told my friend he was overthinking things.
He's been quiet ever since, which I think proves my point.

My gym membership is the only commitment I've successfully maintained.
Mostly because we have an understanding: they don't expect me to show up, and I don't expect them to ask for money.

I'm reading a book about anti-gravity.
I can't put it down.

My parents said I'd thank them one day.
I'm still working out whether it's gratitude or Stockholm syndrome.
My biggest accomplishment this year is that my therapist only cries during our sessions sometimes.
